<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel application. Follow existing conventions; when creating/editing files, check sibling files. Expert packages: inertiajs/inertia-laravel (INERTIA) v2, laravel/fortify (FORTIFY) v1, laravel/framework (LARAVEL) v12, laravel/prompts (PROMPTS) v0, laravel/wayfinder (WAYFINDER) v0, laravel/boost (BOOST) v2, laravel/mcp (MCP) v0, laravel/pail (PAIL) v1, laravel/pint (PINT) v1, laravel/sail (SAIL) v1, pestphp/pest (PEST) v4, phpunit/phpunit (PHPUNIT) v12.

This project has domain-specific skills available. You MUST activate the relevant skill whenever you work in that domain—don't wait until you're stuck.
`wayfinder-development` — Activates whenever referencing backend routes in frontend components. Use when importing from @/actions or @/routes, calling Laravel routes from TypeScript, or working with Wayfinder route functions.
`pest-testing` — Tests applications using the Pest 4 PHP framework. Activates when writing tests, creating unit or feature tests, adding assertions, testing Livewire components, browser testing, debugging test failures, working with datasets or mocking; or when the user mentions test, spec, TDD, expects, assertion, coverage, or needs to verify functionality works.

Use descriptive names for variables and methods. Check for reusable components first. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise in your explanations - focus on what's important rather than explaining obvious details.

Use Laravel Boost MCP tools. Use the `list-artisan-commands` tool when you need to call an Artisan command to double-check the available parameters. Whenever you share a project URL with the user, you should use the `get-absolute-url` tool to ensure you're using the correct scheme, domain/IP, and port. You should use the `tinker` tool when you need to execute PHP to debug code or query Eloquent models directly. Use `database-query` when you only need to read from the database. Use `database-schema` before writing migrations or models. Use `browser-logs` to read browser logs, errors, and exceptions; only recent browser logs are useful—ignore old logs. Use `search-docs` before code changes for version-specific Laravel/ecosystem documentation and updated examples; pass package arrays when known. Use multiple broad, simple topic queries, e.g. `['rate limiting', 'routing rate limiting', 'routing']`; do not add package names. Query syntax: `authentication` auto-stems; `rate limit` means AND; `"infinite scroll"` is exact; `middleware "rate limit"` combines terms; `queries=["authentication", "middleware"]` means ANY.

Always use curly braces for control structures, even for single-line bodies. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()`.
`public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`
Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless the constructor is private. Always use explicit return type declarations and appropriate parameter type hints. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over inline comments. Never use comments within the code itself unless the logic is exceptionally complex. Add useful array shape type definitions when appropriate. Enum keys are typically TitleCase.

The app is served by Laravel Herd at `https?://[kebab-case-project-dir].test`; use `get-absolute-url` for valid URLs. You must not run any commands to make the site available via HTTP(S). It is always available through Laravel Herd.
Every change must be programmatically tested. Write a new test or update an existing test, then run affected tests. Run the minimum: `php artisan test --compact` with a specific filename or filter.
If frontend changes are not reflected, ask the user to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`.

=== inertia-laravel/core ===
Components live in `resources/js/pages` unless `vite.config.js` specifies otherwise. Use `Inertia::render()` instead of Blade views. ALWAYS use `search-docs` for version-specific Inertia documentation.
=== inertia-laravel/v2 ===
Use v1/v2 features; check documentation first. Deferred props require an empty pulsing or animated skeleton. Features include deferred props, infinite scrolling (merging props + `WhenVisible`), lazy loading, polling, and prefetching.

=== laravel/core ===
Use `php artisan make:` to create files; generic PHP classes use `php artisan make:class`. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands and correct `--options`.
Use typed Eloquent relationship methods; prefer relationships and models over raw queries/manual joins and `DB::`; use `Model::query()`. Prevent N+1 with eager loading; use query builder for very complex operations. New models get useful factories and seeders; ask whether more are needed, using `list-artisan-commands` to check `php artisan make:model` options.
For APIs, default to Eloquent API Resources and versioning unless existing routes differ. Always create Form Request classes with validation rules and custom error messages; inspect sibling requests for array/string style. Use built-in authentication/authorization. Prefer named routes and `route()`. Use queued jobs with `ShouldQueue` for time-consuming work. Use environment variables only in configuration files - never use the `env()` function directly outside of config files. Always use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`.
Use factories (including custom states) for test models. Follow existing Faker style (`$this->faker` or `fake()`).
For tests use `php artisan make:test [options] {name}`; pass `--unit` for unit tests; most should be feature tests. If `Illuminate\Foundation\ViteException: Unable to locate file in Vite manifest`, run `npm run build` or ask the user to run `npm run dev` or `composer run dev`.
CRITICAL: ALWAYS use `search-docs` for version-specific Laravel documentation.
Laravel 12 uses streamlined structure: middleware are configured in `bootstrap/app.php` via `Application::configure()->withMiddleware()`; `bootstrap/app.php` registers middleware, exceptions, and routing; `bootstrap/providers.php` contains application providers; `app\Console\Kernel.php` no longer exists—use `bootstrap/app.php` or `routes/console.php`; commands in `app/Console/Commands/` are automatic. Column-modifying migrations must include all previous attributes. Limit eager-loaded records with `$query->latest()->limit(10);`. Casts can use `casts()`; follow existing models.

=== wayfinder/core ===
Import routes from `@/actions/` (controllers) or `@/routes/` (named routes). IMPORTANT: Activate `wayfinder-development` skill whenever referencing backend routes in frontend components.
